title: Introduce Economizer: automated serving recommendations for batching, caching, quantization
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Adds ‘Economizer’ recommendation engine that produces per-route and per-model suggestions for batching, prefix cache policies, and quantization profiles. Includes UI in Console for previewing, canarying, and applying recommendations. Expected typical savings 15-35% on token spend for chat-heavy workloads.

description: Motivation: Customers and internal benchmarks show significant potential savings from better defaults and automated recommendations for batching, prefix caching, and quantization. This PR adds 'Economizer', an offline+online recommendation engine that analyzes historical request traces and live telemetry to propose per-route and per-model serving configuration changes. High-level changes: 1) telemetry ingestion and workload summarizer to compute request size distributions, recurrence of prefixes, and KV-cache hit opportunities; 2) a lightweight scoring policy that trades expected latency impact vs. per-token cost delta to rank candidate batching sizes, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles; 3) a Console UI surface to preview suggestions, run a simulated unit-economics estimate, and trigger a canary application using existing rollout machinery; 4) CLI export for audit and on-prem workflows and a test harness for canary e2e. Single continuous description of commits and files: initial scaffolding (ingest + schema), heuristics for batching and cache suggestion, quantization profile candidate generator (FP16/INT8/LLM-quant variants), integration with model registry to suggest compatible quantizations, Console panel + hook to create a canary rollout, unit economics simulator that replays traces against current vs candidate config and reports projected cost/latency deltas, and CI job that runs economizer integration tests in a nightly bench. Checklist: - [x] Telemetry ingestion pipeline implemented - [x] Workload summarizer and offline scoring - [x] Recommendation policy + profile store - [x] Console UI + preview simulator - [x] Canary application flow using rollout APIs - [x] E2E tests and CI job - [x] Docs and operator guidelines What changed at a glance: added telemetry_collector, summarizer, policy engine, Console components, CLI export, new CI workflow, and docs. Key design notes: - Recommendations are advisory by default; auto-apply is gated behind explicit org-level opt-in with audit logging. - Scoring balances 99p latency impact against per-token cost delta using configurable utility weights; operators can tune sensitivity via Console or configmap. - Quantization suggestions only surface when model in registry has validated compatibility; fallback to less aggressive quantization offered when regression risk is high. - Canary flow uses existing rollout system: small percentage, latency/cost SLO guardrails, automatic rollback on SLA regression. Tests & benchmark summary: Microbenchmarks on a sample chat workload (conv length 6, avg tokens 420/request) show batching + prefix caching + int8 quant suggestion reduced per-token compute cost by ~28% and end-to-end p95 latency increased <5% under our preferred utility weight. Nightly bench across 6 production-like traces yields median projected savings 18% (IQR 12-27%). Safety and rollout: - Default behavior is read-only recommendations surfaced to owners. - Ops can run the simulator which replays anonymized traces for a chosen route to obtain expected cost/latency deltas. - Automatic rollouts require organization opt-in and a successful canary. Review summary and conversation: Initial review by Carlos raised concerns about telemetry cardinality and retention; we added rate-limiting and summarization windows to the collector and documented retention/PII safeguards. Aisha requested clearer guardrails around quantization because of model-regression risk; we added quantization compatibility checks and an explicit fallback bucket plus a forced QA gate for models without prior quantization validation. Evan requested end-to-end integration tests covering rollback paths; added e2e canary test and CI job. CI run history: first pipeline failed on lint in Console component (fixed in commit e5f1b8), then integration tests flaked (timeout) on a noisy runner and were re-run; final CI status passing. Merge decisions: after two approvals and green CI the branch was squashed and merged into main. Impact and rollout plan: Gradual rollout starting with internal beta on low-SLA test tenants for two weeks, then enable read-only recommendations for public beta, followed by org-level opt-in automatic application for Enterprise customers. Ops playbook and runbook included in docs/ops/economizer.md. Estimated economics: For a representative chat customer of 1M tokens/day this can save approximately $250–$900/month depending on workload skew and aggressiveness of quantization choice; on aggregate we expect non-trivial bottom-line improvement for heavy chat workloads. Follow-ups and next steps: - Add reinforcement signal from observed post-change telemetry to close the feedback loop and promote/demote profiles automatically. - Expand quantization validator to run lightweight quality checks using representative prompts. - Add per-tenant sensitivity presets and a policy to auto-suggest based on spend thresholds. Known limitations: - Recommendations rely on historical traces; cold-start routes may have noisy suggestions. - Certain proprietary models without quantization metadata are not supported yet. Files of interest for reviewers: internal/economizer/policy/engine.py contains the scoring heuristic, console/src/components/RecommendationsPanel.tsx shows the UI flow, and tests/e2e/economizer_canary_test.py simulates a canary application and rollback. This PR is intentionally conservative: defaults are suggestions only and we added explicit audit trails and safety gates to minimize customer risk.
review_comments: Carlos Rivera: Please ensure collector has cardinality limits and PII scrubbers; suggest adding a summarization window. Author: added rate-limits and documented scrub rules in collector README.
Aisha Patel: Quantization risk needs a fallback path and an explicit QA gate for models going to INT8. Author: added compatibility checks and a fallback profile; updated docs with QA flow.
Evan Zhang: Add e2e test for rollback path and CI job to catch regressions. Author: added tests/e2e/economizer_canary_test.py and a nightly CI workflow.
